Solder Joint.Type: Metallic connections formed by melting solder to join the transistor leads to the board holes
Solder Joint.Color: Metallic grayish-silver, with some darkened areas due to oxidation or residue
Solder Joint.Size: 1-2mm in diameter at each connection point
Solder Joint.Composition: Melted solder alloy bonded to both the lead and the copper pad inside the hole
Solder Joint.Quantity: Three solder joints, one for each lead of the transistor
Solder Joint.Relative Location: Located at the base of each transistor lead, within the corresponding hole
Solder Joint.Orientation: Circular, conforming to the shape of the hole and lead
Solder Joint.Connection/Attachments: Electrically connects the transistor’s leads to the copper traces via the holes

Perforated Board.Type: Printed circuit board with a grid of holes and copper traces for mounting electronic components
Perforated Board.Color: Copper-colored metallic surface with darkened areas due to oxidation or solder residue, and dark holes
Perforated Board.Size: Visible portion is rectangular with multiple rows and columns of holes, approximately 3cm by 4cm, and multiple vertical columns of holes and traces with overall dimensions not fully visible
Perforated Board.Material: Copper-clad laminate, likely FR-4 (glass fiber reinforced epoxy)
Perforated Board.Composition: Copper conductive layer on a non-conductive substrate with insulating material (typically FR-4) and holes drilled through it
Perforated Board.Relative Location: Occupies the entire visible area of the image and serves as the base substrate for the transistor and copper traces
Perforated Board.Orientation: Horizontal plane with horizontal and vertical grid pattern, flat and horizontal, aligned with the camera’s viewpoint, and vertical copper traces running perpendicular to the board edges
Perforated Board.Connection/Attachments: Provides mounting points and electrical pathways for components like the transistor, and serves as a mounting surface with electrical connections via the copper traces and holes

Copper Trace.Type: Thin, flat conductive pathways etched into the board surface
Copper Trace.Color: Copper-colored, appearing reddish-brown due to oxidation, with some areas darker from oxidation or solder residue
Copper Trace.Size: Width varies between 0.5mm and 1mm; length extends across the board, connecting multiple holes
Copper Trace.Composition: Pure copper or copper alloy, etched into the board surface to form conductive paths
Copper Trace.Quantity: Multiple traces visible, forming a grid pattern with horizontal and vertical lines
Copper Trace.Relative Location: Runs horizontally and vertically, intersecting at the holes where the transistor is mounted, located beneath and surrounding the transistor leads and holes
Copper Trace.Orientation: Horizontal and vertical, forming a grid with horizontal lines running left to right and vertical lines running parallel to each other in columns
Copper Trace.Connection/Attachments: Connected to the holes via solder joints, forming electrical pathways between the transistor and other components

Transistor.Type: Through-hole electronic component with three metallic leads, housed in a black plastic TO-92 style casing
Transistor.Color: Black body with a matte finish and a circular marking containing a 'T' symbol; metallic leads are silver-colored
Transistor.Size: Body approximately 5mm square or 5mm in width and height; leads extend approximately 10mm or about 15mm downward from the body
Transistor.Material: Plastic body; metallic leads made of tin-plated copper or similar conductive alloy
Transistor.Composition: Plastic encapsulation with internal semiconductor material; leads are metal wire or ribbon; body composed of molded plastic housing with a printed marking
Transistor.Relative Location: Centered on the perforated board, positioned between vertical copper traces or mounted on the perforated board
Transistor.Orientation: Body oriented vertically, leads pointing downward and aligned with the copper traces below
Transistor.Connection/Attachments: Leads soldered into three adjacent holes on the perforated board, electrically connecting to the copper traces or forming electrical connections

Hole.Type: Circular openings in the perforated board for component mounting

Hole.Material: Copper-plated metal, with surrounding board material being plastic or fiberglass
Hole.Composition: Metal with a hole drilled or punched through, exposing the copper pad underneath, with solder and possibly flux residue
